correctness.rationale: Proof follows from exact identities \(\frac{d}{dt}[(x^2+y^2)/2]=y^2z\) and \(\dot z=z-(b+y^2-a x^2)\), a valid future-filter integral for bounded solutions, and compact invariant omega-limit rigidity. On any omega orbit with \(y^2z\equiv0\), a nonzero y interval would force \(z=0\) and simultaneously \(a x^2-y^2-b=0\), derivative \(2(a+1)xy=0\); both \(a=-1\) and \(a\ne-1\) cases contradict the ODE. Hence the only such complete bounded orbit is the equilibrium; nontrivial omega sets force strict sign crossings. The actual packaged checker recomputes the nonstandard algebra; no finite run is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Original source numerically identifies very rare hidden bounded motions for positive forcing a. The new exact theorem gives a rigorous globally quantified obstruction in the entire \(a\leq0,\ b>0\) half-plane, plus two unavoidable recurrence sectors and an amplitude threshold for every nonstationary bounded forward orbit whenever it exists. This is a structurally motivated qualitative restriction on the original family rather than an arbitrary finite calculation or a parameter renaming.
